groups.title: Microsoft Ten Immutable Laws of Security (v2, 2017)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If a bad actor can persuade you to run their program on your computer, it's not solely your computer anymore.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If a bad actor can alter the operating system on your computer, it's not your computer anymore.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If a bad actor has unrestricted physical access to your computer, it's not your computer anymore.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If you allow a bad actor to run active content on your website, it's not your website anymore.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Weak passwords trump strong security.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A computer is only as secure as the administrator is trustworthy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Encrypted data is only as secure as its decryption key.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An out-of-date antimalware scanner is only marginally better than no scanner at all.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Absolute anonymity isn't practically achievable, either online or offline.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Technology isn't a panacea.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Attackers don't care.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Ruthless prioritization is a survival skill.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Cybersecurity is a team sport.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Your network isn't as trustworthy as you think it is.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Isolated networks aren't automatically secure.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Encryption alone isn't a data protection solution.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Technology doesn't solve people and process problems.
